findings.title: Denial cache key uses raw underscore concatenation and can collide
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds the cache key as `namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. Because the fields are not length-prefixed or escaped, different tuples containing underscores can map to the same key; for example, `name="a", parent="b_c"` and `name="a_b", parent="c"` both produce a suffix of `a_b_c`. A cached denial for one dashboard/folder can then falsely deny access to a different allowed resource for the same user/action until the TTL expires. Use a collision-resistant key such as a hash of the fields or length-delimited concatenation.

findings.title: Check re-queries permissions for every distinct denied resource
findings.body: After a cached permission map is found but the requested resource is not allowed, `Check` unconditionally falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which queries the permission store. The subsequent denial cache only prevents repeats for the exact `name`+`parent` tuple. For a user with a cached empty or stale permission map, each unique `Name` causes a fresh DB permissions query. This allows sequential requests with arbitrary unique resource names to bypass the action-level permission cache and impose significant DB load. Consider rate-limiting or deduplicating these fallbacks, or using a per-action last-refresh/negative TTL instead of a full DB query per denied resource.

findings.title: Remote AuthZ client still caches decisions and bypasses the server-side fix
findings.body: `newRemoteRBACClient` still configures `authzlib.NewClient` with a 30-second local cache. The PR disables the authlib client cache only for the in-process path via `NoopCache`. In remote/standalone deployments, `Check`/`List` results, including false denials, can be served from this client-side cache and never reach the server-side denial-cache and DB requery logic. Users in those modes can therefore still be denied access to newly created dashboards/folders for up to 30 seconds. If the fix is intended for all modes, the remote client cache needs to be disabled, shortened, or invalidated on resource creation.
